cards.title: LHI
cards.subtitle: Labour Heat Index
cards.why: Labour conditions are broadly neutral, with no decisive directional labour signal.
cards.summary: Labour conditions are broadly neutral, with no decisive directional labour signal. Initial claims is the strongest USD-supportive input, while JOLTS quits is the largest drag.

drivers.name: Initial claims
drivers.info: Weekly initial unemployment-insurance claims. Lower claims generally indicate a firmer labour market, so MacroLens inverts this series.
drivers.detail: Normalized labour signal +1.37; equal-weight contribution across 5 available labour inputs.

drivers.name: JOLTS quits
drivers.info: JOLTS quits rate. A higher quits rate can indicate worker confidence and a tighter labour market.
drivers.detail: Normalized labour signal -1.16; equal-weight contribution across 5 available labour inputs.

drivers.name: JOLTS openings
drivers.info: JOLTS job openings, reported in thousands. Higher openings generally indicate stronger labour demand.
drivers.detail: Normalized labour signal -0.87; equal-weight contribution across 5 available labour inputs.

drivers.name: NFP surprise
drivers.info: Nonfarm payroll surprise: actual payroll growth minus the market consensus forecast, measured in thousands of jobs.
drivers.detail: Normalized labour signal +0.73; equal-weight contribution across 5 available labour inputs.

drivers.name: Unemployment
drivers.info: US unemployment rate. MacroLens inverts this input: lower unemployment is treated as a firmer labour signal and higher unemployment as a weaker one.
drivers.detail: Normalized labour signal -0.43; equal-weight contribution across 5 available labour inputs.

cards.title: IMS
cards.subtitle: Inflation Momentum Score
cards.why: Inflation momentum is moderately cooling, reducing USD support through the macro layer.
cards.summary: Inflation momentum is moderately cooling, reducing USD support through the macro layer. Core PPI is the strongest USD-supportive input, while Core CPI momentum is the largest drag.

drivers.name: Core CPI momentum
drivers.info: Three-month annualised momentum in core CPI, which excludes food and energy. MacroLens compares it with its own recent history rather than using the raw level alone.

drivers.name: Core PPI
drivers.info: Core producer-price index level, normalized against its five-year history to measure unusual producer-price pressure.

drivers.name: Core PCE momentum
drivers.info: Three-month annualised momentum in core PCE, the Federal Reserve's preferred underlying inflation gauge.

drivers.name: Inflation diffusion
drivers.info: Share of the tracked inflation components whose momentum is rising. Broad acceleration increases the inflation score; broad cooling reduces it.

cards.title: RDS
cards.subtitle: Rate Differential Signal
cards.why: Relative-rate momentum materially leans against the USD.
cards.summary: Relative-rate momentum materially leans against the USD. MacroLens scores the recent change in US-versus-German rate advantages, not the absolute spread alone. The largest drag comes from US–Germany 10Y spread movement.

drivers.name: US–Germany 10Y spread movement
drivers.info: Change in the US-Germany 10-year yield spread. A widening US advantage is USD-supportive; a narrowing advantage is USD-negative.

drivers.name: US curve-slope movement
drivers.info: Change in the US 10-year minus 2-year yield-curve slope. This is a smaller contextual component of the Rate Differential Signal.

drivers.name: US–Germany 2Y spread movement
drivers.info: Change in the US-Germany 2-year yield spread. The model cares about whether the US short-rate advantage is widening or narrowing, not simply whether the absolute spread is positive.

technical_data.name: US–Germany 2Y spread movement
technical_data.info: Change in the US-Germany 2-year yield spread. The model cares about whether the US short-rate advantage is widening or narrowing, not simply whether the absolute spread is positive.

technical_data.name: US–Germany 10Y spread movement
technical_data.info: Change in the US-Germany 10-year yield spread. A widening US advantage is USD-supportive; a narrowing advantage is USD-negative.

cards.title: PES
cards.subtitle: Policy Expectation Score
cards.why: Current Federal Reserve expectations provide strong support to the USD outlook.
cards.summary: Current Federal Reserve expectations provide strong support to the USD outlook. USD support is led by Fed funds futures.

drivers.name: Fed funds futures
drivers.info: Fed funds futures imply the market's expected Federal Reserve policy path around upcoming FOMC meetings. MacroLens compares that path with its recent baseline; fewer expected cuts or implied hikes are USD-supportive. This component is normalized as a z-score, so unusually strong policy pricing can exceed ±1 before it is combined with the communication stance.
drivers.detail: Policy-pricing signal derived from the futures-implied path relative to its rolling baseline.

drivers.name: Fed communication stance
drivers.info: Current Federal Reserve communication stance. In the present methodology, a hawkish stance adds +0.20, a dovish stance subtracts 0.20 and a neutral stance adds zero.
drivers.detail: Communication-stance adjustment used by the current PES methodology.

cards.title: Sentiment
cards.subtitle: Equity Risk Sentiment
cards.why: Equity risk sentiment is currently classified as Risk Off.
cards.summary: Equity risk sentiment is currently classified as Risk Off. VIX is the strongest risk-on input, while Put / Call Ratio provides the largest risk-off offset. Risk sentiment is displayed separately as supporting market context, while the crowding overlay is driven by USD positioning.

cards.title: Crowding
cards.subtitle: USD Crowding Overlay
cards.why: USD crowding is classified as Neutral at +0.097.
cards.summary: USD crowding is classified as Neutral at +0.097. In the V1 final-bias formula this positioning score is applied as a dampener through the -Crowding term.

drivers.name: USD positioning / crowding
drivers.info: The current USD positioning score used as the crowding overlay. In the V1 final-bias formula, positive crowding subtracts from the final score and negative crowding adds to it.
drivers.detail: This row shows its direct contribution to the final score at the 20% final-bias weight.
